title: Coding agent
blurb: A tool-using agent edits a small repo: model calls, a clock tool, file writes, a notification. Workspace snapshotted before every call.
summary: An agent was asked to add a greeting endpoint to a small repository. It asked the model for an answer, saved it to a file, asked the model to review it, saved the review, and sent a notification. The model here is a test model that answers with random words, so every live run is different, which is exactly the problem Khonsu solves.

story.text: The agent read the clock through a recorded tool. On replay the same timestamp comes back, so time-dependent code behaves identically.
The first model call: the task goes in, an answer comes out. Select it to see the full prompt and response.
The agent wrote out/answer.md. The workspace panel marks it as new at this call, and clicking it shows exactly what was written.
It saved the recorded timestamp to out/meta.json.
The second model call reviews the answer. Its prompt contains the answer from call #1, so if #1 ever changes, this call changes too.
The review was written to out/review.md.
A notification: an external side effect. On replay it is not sent again; the recorded result is returned instead.
All of it is one small file: 7 calls and 9 snapshots of the repository, protected by a hash chain (the "integrity verified" chip).

title: Same task, re-run
blurb: The same agent and task run again live. Compare it with the first run to see where they diverge.
summary: The same agent and the same task as Coding agent, run a second time live. Nothing in the code changed, yet the run is different: the model sampled a different answer, and everything that depends on it changed too.

story.text: The clock reads a different time: this was a new live run.
Same prompt, different answer. This is where the two runs first diverge.
The review prompt is different too, because it contains the answer from call #1.
Open Coding agent from Examples and press "Compare with a re-run": Khonsu lines the two runs up call by call and points at the first divergence and the exact JSON field.

title: Fork at call #4
blurb: khonsu fork: calls 0–3 replayed from the recording (hollow marks), the review regenerated live.
summary: Made with `khonsu fork coding-agent.khn@4`: go back to call #4 of the Coding agent run and let the future play out again. The files were restored as they were at the start, calls #0–#3 came from the recording (no model, no cost), and the agent went live from #4.

story.text: Calls #0 to #3 are hollow on the dial: they were served from the original recording, byte for byte.
The first answer is identical to the original run's, because it was replayed rather than sampled again.
The fork point: from here the model was called for real, and it wrote a new review.
The new review was saved; compare the file with the original run's.
The notification was really sent this time, because it came after the fork point.
The fork is saved as its own recording that remembers its parent (see "parent" in the header).

title: Streaming + parallel
blurb: Tool call, a streamed answer (with chunk timing), and three concurrent requests.
summary: A different agent that uses function calling and streaming, then fires three requests at the same time.

story.text: The model asked the agent to call get_weather. The request, the tool-call arguments, and the model's choice are all recorded.
The final answer was streamed token by token. The token-stream chart shows when each chunk arrived, and replay can reproduce that timing.
Calls #2 to #4 were sent at the same moment. Khonsu matches requests by their content, so they replay correctly in any order.
This agent has no workspace, so the file panel is empty: recording works with or without one.
